name: sol_heuristics_7
description: Off-by-one error in comparison, loop bound, or array indexing logic
question: The source file in `source` contains a comparison operator, loop boundary, or index calculation involving array/list length that is off by one (e.g., using `<=` where `<` is required, or vice versa, or starting/ending an iteration one position too early or late), causing an out-of-bounds access, skipped element, or incorrect boundary condition with a security or correctness impact, excluding cases where the boundary is intentional and correct for the documented semantics.
criteria: A loop iterates with `for (i = 0; i <= array.length; i++)` and indexes `array[i]`, causing an out-of-bounds read on the last iteration
A loop meant to process all elements starts at index 1 instead of 0, silently skipping the first element (e.g., `for (i = 1; i < list.length; i++)`)
A balance or allowance check uses `amount <= balance` where the intended safe condition is `amount < balance`, allowing draining beyond the intended limit
An index variable is set to `list.length` instead of `list.length - 1` when accessing the last element, causing an out-of-bounds access
A vesting/deadline comparison uses `block.timestamp <= endTime` instead of `block.timestamp < endTime`, allowing an action one unit past the intended cutoff
